paths.description: Homepage and search/discovery entry point; represents the primary landing template.
Wonderwall lyric detail and media/player surface; represents the primary content task.
Oasis artist detail; represents entity/detail navigation.
Most-accessed songs; represents long listing/index pages.
Subscription call-to-action destination; represents the commercial flow. It redirected to the homepage.
Deliberately unknown route used to inspect the HTTP/error recovery surface.

findings.summary: The consent interface breaks the mobile viewport and makes its actions hard to reach.
findings.evidence: At 360x800, layout captures on all five templates report 586 to 598 px of horizontal overflow. The mobile song screenshot shows the consent panel beginning at x=221 with action buttons clipped beyond the right edge.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the consent surface width fluid with max-inline-size: min(100% - 2rem, ...), wrap content and actions, and test it at 320 to 400 CSS px without changing the layout viewport.

findings.summary: A blocking consent interstitial obscures the core content on every audited path.
findings.evidence: Initial screenshots of the homepage, song, artist, listing, plan destination, and 404 all show a large modal covering the primary content before any interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, accessible consent surface that keeps essential content available, provides equal accept and reject actions, and preserves a clear way to revisit choices.

findings.summary: Animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matched, the preference probe still found four running skeletonAnimation instances at 500 ms and found no prefers-reduced-motion rule in accessible page CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a reduced-motion media query that removes non-essential skeleton and transition animation while preserving immediate state feedback.

findings.summary: Route and state changes have no View Transition integration.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection across the representative templates found no view-transition CSS or navigation opt-in, while the site exposes many cross-document routes and interactive states.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin navigation with cross-document View Transitions and a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long lyric and listing pages do not expose scroll-state-aware navigation chrome.
findings.evidence: The long song and listing templates have fixed header/navigation structures, but inspected CSS contains no scroll-state container query or scroll progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or scrolled-state treatment for long lyrics and rankings, with reduced-motion support.

findings.summary: Overlay positioning does not use anchor positioning or fallback positions.
findings.evidence: The rendered page exposes hundreds of role=tooltip and role=button nodes from site and consent UI, but CSS/DOM inspection found no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning with position-try fallbacks for menus and tooltips where browser support permits, retaining the current placement as fallback.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is slow on both primary templates.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP at 7.5 s on the homepage and 11.1 s on the song page, with performance scores of 0.62 and 0.59. The desktop trace still measured song LCP at 2.96 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Identify the LCP element, make it discoverable from initial HTML, prioritise it, and defer ad/CMP and other non-critical work until after primary content.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused code and ad-related script weight.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 455 KiB unused JavaScript and 67 KiB unused CSS. The homepage HAR transferred 1.12 MB of script, including ad, tag-manager and consent dependencies.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split template features, remove unused styles, and load advertising, analytics, and consent vendor modules only after the relevant choice or idle boundary.

findings.summary: Form controls and accessibility structure contain label and role failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports unlabelled form controls on both pages, visible-label/accessibility-name mismatch on home, and invalid list structure. The song probe found ten unlabelled controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each interactive control a programmatic label matching its visible text, repair list semantics, and verify the accessibility tree with axe and screen-reader smoke tests.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast audits fail on both homepage and song templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground and surface tokens to meet WCAG contrast in every theme, including dimmed and consent states.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated and many controls are too small.
findings.evidence: Programmatically focusing the first visible button produced outline: none and no box shadow on all probes. Lighthouse fails target-size on the song page, and the probe counted 63 rendered interactive targets below 24 px in one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible treatment and enlarge or space touch targets to at least the WCAG target-size floor, preferably 44 CSS px for primary controls.

findings.summary: Important browser security headers and cookie protections are missing.
findings.evidence: The headers probe found no CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. Six of ten cookies were flagged insecure; analytics and consent cookies use SameSite=None without Secure and some persist for 390 to 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and mark every SameSite=None cookie Secure. Shorten analytics/consent retention where possible.

findings.summary: Third-party tracking dominates the initial network load before a choice is made.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe found 15 third-party origins and four known tracker domains. The homepage HAR attributes 55 of 59 requests and 1.48 MB of 1.50 MB transferred to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential analytics and advertising until consent, reduce vendors, batch necessary telemetry, and set a strict third-party request/byte budget.

findings.summary: Images lack responsive delivery and reserved dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image probe found 22 homepage images without dimensions, 22 without srcset, 37 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 3 oversized images, and no modern-format images. The song page has 14 of 15 images without dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions, srcset/sizes, below-fold lazy loading, and AVIF/WebP variants while preserving eager high-priority loading for the LCP image only.

findings.summary: The app advertises installability but has no active service worker or offline fallback.
findings.evidence: A standalone web app manifest with start_url and icons is linked, but both navigator.serviceWorker.controller and getRegistrations() were empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Register a small service worker that precaches an offline shell and preserves previously opened lyrics, with network-first updates when connectivity returns.

findings.summary: The prominent subscription journey does not reach subscription information.
findings.evidence: The audited Assine destination /planos.html ended at the homepage, with homepage title, canonical URL and content. The user receives neither pricing nor an explanation or recovery path.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the subscription route stable, show pricing and commitments before sign-in/payment, and provide an explicit error/retry state if plans cannot be loaded.

findings.summary: Modal and transient UI is represented with custom role-based structures instead of native primitives.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM contains four role=dialog regions and hundreds of role-based controls/tooltips, but probes found zero native dialog, popover, or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate modal flows to dialog and transient menus/tooltips to popover, preserving focus management and light-dismiss behaviour.

findings.summary: Reusable content components rely on page-level layout rather than container responsiveness.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across home, song, artist and listing templates found no @container or container-type usage despite cards and ranking components appearing in differently sized regions.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable cards, rankings and player controls where their available inline size differs from the viewport.

findings.summary: The first consent layer presents acceptance but no equally direct rejection action.
findings.evidence: The initial consent screenshot offers a prominent Consent button and Manage options, but no Reject all action. Rejecting requires additional navigation while accepting is one click.
findings.suggestedFix: Place equally prominent Accept all and Reject all actions on the first layer, with granular management as a third option.

findings.summary: No explicit high-contrast or forced-colors adaptation was found.
findings.evidence: prefers-contrast: more matched in the probe, but accessible CSS contained no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules; Lighthouse also found baseline contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adjustments for essential controls, outlines and scroll affordances, and avoid suppressing system colors.

findings.summary: Carousel and horizontal browsing surfaces do not expose declarative snap behaviour.
findings.evidence: The homepage presents carousel-like featured and playlist regions, but inspected CSS contains no scroll-snap or related declarative gesture treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use overflow scrolling with CSS scroll snap and platform overscroll behaviour for horizontal card rails, retaining button controls for keyboard users.

taskList.title: Repair the consent experience on mobile and stop it obscuring core content
Cut LCP, unused code, and third-party startup cost
Fix labels, contrast, focus visibility, and target sizing
Harden response headers and cookie attributes
Restore the subscription destination and transparent pricing path
Add responsive image delivery and intrinsic dimensions
Add an offline fallback for the installable experience
Progressively enhance navigation, positioning and reusable component responsiveness
